subject: Question about Stan syntax for function calling and ODE solving

messages.author: bacb0402e67daa77
messages.subject: Question about Stan syntax for function calling and ODE solving
parts:
I would like to define a set of ODE's to be called by a gain function and am not sure about the most efficient way to go about this. 
Here is a simplified version of what I have for now:

functions {
        real[] inhibition(real S1,
                          real S2, 
                          real A1,
                          real A2,
                          real B1,
                          real B2,
                          real G1,
                          real G2,
                          real[] duhatdt){
        duhatdt[1] <- (A1 * S1 + A2 * duhatdt[1] - B1 * uhat[2] - B2 * uhat[1]) / (1 + G1 * uhat[2] + G2 * uhat[1])
        duhatdt[2] <- (A1 * S2 + A2 * duhatdt[2] - B1 * uhat[1] - B2 * uhat[2]) / (1 + G1 * uhat[1] + G2 * uhat[2])
        return duhatdt;
        }

        real[] gain(real t,
                    real cs1,
                    real cs2,
                    real cs3,
                    real cs4,
                    real cs0,
                    real[] x){
        duhatdt <- fmax(0,cs1 * x + cs2 * x ^ 2 + cs3 * x ^ 3 + cs4 * x ^ 4 + cs0);
        return duhatdt;
        }
}

where x = inhibition(real S1, real S2, real A1, real A2, real B1, real B2, real G1, real G2, real[] duhatdt).

However, looking at the example code on page 163 of the manual, I wasn't sure how I would then invoke the functions when using integrate_ode in the model block of the code.

Thanks for your help.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Question about Stan syntax for function calling and ODE solving
parts:
I don't know what a gain function is, but I can answer in general.

The ODE system function to compute derivatives has to have exactly
the signature given in the manual.

So you need to put all the data variables into either a real or int
array and all the parameters into a real array for the call.

We may add more flexible ways to do this in the future after we have
more experience ourselves with the current setup.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Question about Stan syntax for function calling and ODE solving
parts:
I'm not sure what you mean by "put in a function in the ODE solver".
You need to define a function for the system derivatives. You can
call other functions from the system function, and you can write a function
that calls integrate_ode if you want. In general, arguments can be function
calls.

- Bob
